name: Reverse Box Turn (forward half)
notes: Owner's description (2026-11-16): the Box Turn with everything reversed. The turn is to the left; the lead starts forward on the left foot, side on the right, close the left. The mirror image of Box Turn (forward half); no rise. Usually followed by Reverse Box Turn (backward half). Called the Left Box Turn in the American syllabus; the International Reverse Turn is a different, progressive figure. Turn timing from the book (2026-11-17, a box-step study card): the partner going forward "commences to turn" on 1, turns 1/8 between 1 and 2 and 1/8 between 2 and 3; the partner going back turns 1/4 between 1 and 2, "body turns less", and the body completes the turn on 3. Written that way (2026-11-17): the bodies turn 1/24 left on count 1 (the turn commencing), 1/8 on count 2 and 1/12 on the close, a quarter in all, and the close's turn is carried back into count 2's foot placement. The lead goes forward, so the couple turns round the follow (the default turning centre), and count 2 is written as her step, as the lead would describe it. Step sizes, provisional, chosen by measuring the 3D body solver against every figure check, including "own feet" (each dancer's footprints may not overlap): count 1 is 0.4 forward and 0.3 to the left; count 2 is 0.6 forward and 0.3 to the left. Strides: 0.43, 0.80 and 0.50 for the lead and 0.50, 0.67 and 0.11 for the follow; the hips sink at most 0.14 m. Not drawn yet (2026-11-17): the book's "body turns less" for the follow, written as `pointing` her count-2 foot a further eighth round; with the foot pointed even a sixteenth further, its toes land on the other foot (the "own feet" check), so the feet point with the body for now. History: the owner's first version put the whole quarter on count 2 with no turn on count 1; the partner on the outside of the turn then lunged round (backward halves, hips sinking up to 0.78 m) or the partner on the inside crossed her feet (forward halves, a foot landing 0.28 on the wrong side of the other), and the forward halves skipped the "crossed feet" and "partner spacing" checks.
